$comment: Agent state: the backlog and its status. One feature is 'in_progress' at a time. Update `status` and `evidence` in the same change that lands the work — never ahead of it. See CLAUDE.md > Definition of done.

features.name: Make the library publishable to npm as @art-tools/react-gantt
features.description: The library has never been published. It is `private: true`, has no license, no repository metadata, and no build guard — a publish from a clean checkout would ship an empty tarball because `dist/` is gitignored and nothing forces a build. Rename from the unowned two-character `@am` scope to `@art-tools/react-gantt`, add the missing manifest metadata and an MIT license, fix the exports map so no condition escapes `dist/`, and wire up Changesets plus GitHub Actions with npm provenance. Nothing is published as part of this work.
doneCriteria: `packages/react-gantt/package.json` is not private, is named @art-tools/react-gantt, and carries publishConfig.access public, license, repository (with `directory`), homepage, bugs, keywords, engines
A `prepublishOnly` script rebuilds `dist` — a publish from a fresh clone cannot ship an empty tarball
MIT LICENSE exists at the repo root and inside packages/react-gantt
No `exports` condition points outside `dist/`; `files` is exactly ["dist"]
`npm pack --dry-run` lists dist/**, package.json, README.md, LICENSE and nothing else — no src/, no tests, no tsconfig
`publint` and `@arethetypeswrong/cli` both report no errors
Changesets is configured with a pending initial changeset; `pnpm changeset status` is clean
CI and release workflows exist under .github/workflows/
No occurrence of the old `@am/react-gantt` specifier survives outside dist/ and node_modules
./init.sh passes and its real output is in progress.md
features.blockedBy: Every doneCriteria entry is satisfied except the last: `./init.sh` still exits 1 at `pnpm format:check` on packages/react-gantt/README.md. That failure predates this work (feature `baseline-format-debt`) and is not caused by it — lint, check-types, test and build are all green, and format:check was reduced back from 6 failing files to the same 1 it failed on before. Clear `baseline-format-debt` and this feature is done with no further code change.
features.evidence: Recorded 2026-08-21. pnpm lint: 0 errors, 1 warning (pre-existing clsx default-import in TaskResizer.tsx:1). pnpm check-types: 5/5 workspaces pass. pnpm test: 485 passed across 43 files. pnpm build: 3/3 tasks successful, including both consumer apps. pnpm format:check: 1 file fails (packages/react-gantt/README.md) — pre-existing, see blockedBy. publint: 'All good!'. @arethetypeswrong/cli --exclude-entrypoints style.css: 'No problems found', green on node10/node16-CJS/node16-ESM/bundler. npm pack --dry-run: 11 files, 256.5 kB packed — LICENSE, README.md, package.json, dist/{index.cjs,index.mjs,index.d.ts,index.d.cts,style.css,style.css.d.ts} and two .js.map; no src/, tests, or tsconfig. changeset status: one pending minor for @art-tools/react-gantt.

features.name: Decide the "use client" story for published consumers
features.description: The library ships no "use client" directives; the comment in apps/docs/next.config.ts is explicit that every demo owns its own client boundary. That works for demos in this repo, where each page adds the directive itself. An external Next.js App Router consumer who imports <Gantt /> into a server component gets a confusing server-component error instead of a clear one. Surfaced while preparing the npm release (npm-publish-readiness) and deliberately left alone: adding directives changes behaviour and needs an ADR first. Decide between banner-injecting "use client" at the top of the bundle, marking only the entry, or documenting the wrapper requirement and leaving the code as-is.
doneCriteria: An ADR records the choice and what was rejected — in particular why the library does or does not take on the client boundary for its consumers
If directives are added, the CJS and ESM bundles both carry them and the existing apps/docs demos still work unchanged
packages/react-gantt/README.md states plainly what an App Router consumer has to do
The rationale comment in apps/docs/next.config.ts is updated if the reasoning it records stops being true
./init.sh passes

features.name: Fix the dangling keyboard-navigation roadmap link
features.description: packages/react-gantt/README.md:502 says the widget is 'not yet keyboard-operable — see [Roadmap](#1-keyboard-navigation)', but the Roadmap section has no keyboard-navigation entry; #1 is Critical path. Either restore a keyboard-navigation roadmap entry or retarget the link. Decide which, don't silently drop the accessibility caveat.
doneCriteria: No link in packages/react-gantt/README.md points at a heading that does not exist in that file
The a11y section still states plainly that pointer-only affordances are not keyboard-operable
pnpm format:check passes on the file

features.name: Critical path (CPM) analysis and highlighting
features.description: Layer critical-path analysis on the dependency graph already built by buildDependencyGraph in packages/react-gantt/src/core/scheduling.ts. Compute the longest zero-slack chain, expose a `highlightCriticalPath` option, and surface an ownerState flag so critical bars and links can be styled through the existing slot API. Roadmap item 1 in packages/react-gantt/README.md.
doneCriteria: Slack is computed from working time, not calendar days (ADR-006 — lag is working time)
`highlightCriticalPath` defaults to off; charts that do not set it render byte-identically to today
Critical bars and links expose an ownerState flag; no new hardcoded colors outside the CSS custom properties in packages/react-gantt/src/index.css
Unit tests in packages/react-gantt/src/tests/core/ cover: a linear chain, a diamond (two parallel branches, one critical), a chain crossing non-working time, and a graph with no dependencies
A new ADR records the slack definition and what was rejected
docs/glossary.md gains 'Slack' and 'Critical path' if those terms enter the code
./init.sh passes

features.name: Export and print mode
features.description: Export the chart to PNG/SVG/PDF, plus a print render mode that temporarily disables virtualization and renders the full extent so the browser's print pipeline captures every row. Roadmap item 2 in packages/react-gantt/README.md.
doneCriteria: Print mode is opt-in and scoped to the render pass; it never mutates task data
Un-virtualized rendering is bounded or explicitly documented as O(rows) memory — a 100k-row print must fail loudly, not hang the tab
Exercised against the 100k-row example in apps/docs and the apps/playground large-dataset generator
An ADR records why virtualization is bypassed rather than made print-aware
./init.sh passes

features.name: Keyboard operation of the grid and bars
features.description: The widget's ARIA structure is complete (treegrid + grid, absolute aria-rowindex under virtualization) but bar move, resize, progress and dependency creation are pointer-only, and are deliberately aria-hidden with tabIndex -1 rather than advertised as controls no key can activate. Making them keyboard-operable means giving each a real key handler and then un-hiding it. Blocked on a decision about roving tabindex vs. an application-mode grid.
features.blockedBy: No decision yet on the focus model (roving tabindex across a virtualized treegrid vs. application mode). Write that ADR before writing code — it determines nearly every other choice here.
doneCriteria: An ADR fixes the focus model before implementation starts
Focus survives virtualization: scrolling a focused row out of the window must not silently drop focus to body
Every affordance un-hidden from the a11y tree is genuinely operable by key
The a11y section of packages/react-gantt/README.md is updated to match reality
./init.sh passes
